name: GitHub
diffReason: Easy: registering an OAuth app is self-serve, and review applies only to an optional GitHub Marketplace listing

steps.t: Pick OAuth App or GitHub App
steps.d: GitHub Apps get fine-grained permissions and GitHub generally prefers them; OAuth Apps act only on behalf of the user.
Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App. Enter the application name, homepage URL and callback URL.
Paste your redirect URI, e.g. https://yourapp.com/api/auth/callback/github. You can add up to 10.
Use the client ID and client secret GitHub gives your app, and store the secret securely, for example as an env var.

blockers.s: Organizations with OAuth app access restrictions must approve your app before it can reach their private data.

agent: Draft app name, homepage and description
Generate the correct callback URL for your stack
Check your scopes are the minimum needed
you: Ask org admins to approve, if restricted
sources: Differences between GitHub Apps and OAuth apps
Best practices for creating an OAuth app

checklist.answer: Go to Settings, then Developer settings, then OAuth Apps, and click New OAuth App. You can register it under your personal account or an organization.
OAuth apps act only on behalf of a user. GitHub Apps can act as a user or on their own, use finer permissions, and are generally preferred by GitHub.
The form asks for Application name, Homepage URL and Authorization callback URL. A description is optional, and you can add up to 10 callback URLs.
With wildcard matching off, the redirect URL must match a callback URL exactly. With it on, the host and port must match and the path can be a subdirectory.
GitHub gives you a client ID and a client secret. The secret is needed to get access tokens, except with the device flow. PKCE is supported, with the S256 method only.
Each scope grants a named level of access. repo grants full access to repositories, and with no scope a token only gets read-only access to public information.
A review only comes up if you list the app on GitHub Marketplace, where you can request a review by an onboarding expert.
A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.
